#1454. Russell must do something wacky now after disappointing Bahrain GP qualifying

Never mind the lack of an ice vest, George Russell is somehow going to need to be the coolest man in Malaysia if he is to turn seventh on the grid into a positive result in Sunday’s Bahrain Grand Prix.The first race in Sepang in nearly a decade – a late addition to the calendar because of the conflict in the Middle East – promises to be an absolute scorcher. It might even be worth setting your alarm for the 8am UK start time. Red Bull’s Max Verstappen will start in pole position for the first time this year. He will have Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton alongside him.

It will be the first time since Hungary 2023 that those two gladiators have started on a front row together. Throw in sweltering temperatures, low grip, high tyre degradation, and the ever-present threat of a Malaysian monsoon sweeping through Sepang, and you have the potential for fireworks.

Russell might need something wacky if he is to do anything from that far back. This was a desperately disappointing result for the British driver. After his victory in Baku last weekend, Russell was hopeful he had finally found the winning formula and that he could continue to take the fight to his team-mate Kimi Antonelli, whom he trails in the drivers’ championship by 66pts.

Eighth, four places behind, and 0.24sec slower than the Italian, was not what Russell would have had in mind, although both Mercedes drivers will rise a spot because of the five-place grid penalty meted out to Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar for exceeding his engine allowance for the season.Russell will have felt particularly disappointed as Antonelli only got one run in Q3 after using up a set of soft tyres when he made a mistake and went off track in Q2. He now trails his team mate nine-seven in qualifying head-to-head this year.“No to be honest,” Russell admitted when asked whether he knew why he was so slow. “This circuit is an outlier in terms of the abrasiveness of the tarmac.“The lap times seven years ago were six or seven seconds faster and at certain points on the track it feels like you are driving on gravel, which is the same for everyone, but it is clearly affecting us more than others.”Mercedes’ lack of performance was doubly unexpected because not only did they arrive here with a massive upgrade package, but Russell revealed this week that he and Antonelli were foregoing the cooling vests you see some drivers sporting on the grid, in favour of car performance.

Toto Wolff, the Mercedes team principal, admitted it was a head-scratcher. “Very difficult to understand,” the Austrian said. “We have been a little bit caught out on Friday with some car behaviour that we did not see all year, but then you can say it is very hot and the tarmac is different to all the [other] tracks. It looked really good this morning. We seemed to have, at least with Kimi, made a step in understanding. And then, qualifying was a little bit back to what we saw before, just no performance.”

Still, both titles are in the bag so Wolff cannot be too unhappy. Russell is the one who will be really miffed. He really needs to be beating his team-mate pretty much every race weekend if he is to get his title hopes back on track.

At the front, the mood was somewhat different. Verstappen became the first non-Mercedes-powered pilot to take a pole position this year. It was a first pole position for Red Bull Powertrains, too. And with his long run pace looking more than decent, Verstappen should really hold on for his first win of 2026. Hamilton will do his best to hang on to the Dutchman’s coattails. The seven-time champion was delighted when told he had taken P2. “Let’s go guys! Finally! Great job guys, really great job. Car felt great.”

This was indeed an excellent performance from the Ferrari man – and just the tonic for the Scuderia after weeks of gossip and speculation. Hamilton was admittedly three tenths slower than his rival, which he put purely down to a power deficit on the straights, but he said he was hopeful his long run pace was more competitive. The last time a F1 held a race was held here back in 2017, the British driver claimed pole only to be overhauled by a youthful Verstappen. He will be desperate to turn the tables this time.

“It was really hard to find a good balance, and we made one change before qualifying and we hit the sweet spot,” he reflected afterwards. “I am so, so grateful. I will try my best to hold on to Max tomorrow, and if we are in the fight that would be awesome. I’ve been talking too much, but I guess you talk more when you are happy. It was my best lap of the year. It feels like I won, and I will give it everything tomorrow.”

It is Russell, though, who needs a result even more badly if he is to remain a factor in the championship. “As a team, we have yet to have a bad race this whole season and this was clearly a very bad qualifying for us,” he admitted, adding that “all the numbers” from the upgrade package suggested it was an improvement on the old car. “But I think there is going to be a lot happening tomorrow. The tyre deg is huge and race pace will be king. So even though today was a real disappointment it is not the be all and end all.”

No. 1 ☝️#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/01PqrckQS9

Tomorrow’s race will be the first time since Hungary 2023 that Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton will start on the front row together. It is a reasonable run down to turn one and there are overtaking opportunities through the first few corners at Sepang, with it being similar to the configuration in China, with plenty of lines and moves on offer.

Respect between two great champions 🤩#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/fbZ6aoKRyw

“Very difficult to understand. We have been a little bit caught out on Friday with some car behaviour that we did not see all year, but then you can say it is very hot and the tarmac is the different to all the (other) tracks. It looked really good this morning. We seemed to have, at least with Kimi [Antonelli], made a step in understanding. And then, qualifying was a little bit back to what we saw before, just no performance.”

On Kimi Antonelli’s track limits breach in Q2:

“Not good, because Q2 you know you are going to get through. You lose a set [of softs] in a qualifying that is so tight, where we are on the back foot. That is not good.”

Lewis Hamilton says this is the biggest crowd he has ever seen at Sepang, thanking the fans for making it here today. That is actually a bigger compliment than many watching at home may realise. The traffic this weekend has been horrendous. After 10 years without a race in Malaysia, during which time F1 has grown massively, I think they have forgotten how to do traffic management. Shuttles are inconsistent, taxis can’t get in/out, it’s taking forever just to reach the airport a few kilometres away - some fans have been braving the heat and walking. It took over two hours to get back into Kuala Lumpur last night (48km). My understanding is the Bahrainis are organising the race this year, while local forces are handling the traffic outside the circuit.

“The car has been very good since last week. It is good to come back [from his wrist injury] at such a time and I am enjoying it, fighting for the top three. Even though it was not my finest qualifying session it is a good feeling.

“It is a bit unfortunate we take a penalty on a track where we are that fast but, from eighth, I am confident we can come through the field and come back for a good result.”

“I love this energy [from the crowd]. Big, big thank you to Malaysia for welcoming us. It is so hot here. I keep saying it, but that has made it a massive challenge for the tyres, the car, the mechanics in the garage. I am really, really thankful to my team. We made so many changes through all these practice sessions. Because the cars are sliding, the tyres are overheating, it was really hard to find a good balance, and we made one last change going into qualifying and I think we hit the sweet spot. To be able to close the gap to two or three tenths to Max [Verstappen], who has been so quick all weekend, is great, and I am so grateful.

“I am much happier with where the car is, but tomorrow is a completely different ballgame. Making these tyres last around this track, they are overheating from the get-go. Every little bit of wheelspin you have, every little snap you have makes a difference of how far you are going to go. I like to think we have got a good balance. Max was really quick on his long runs, so I will just try my best to hold onto him tomorrow.”

A reminder that Isack Hadjar will drop from third to eighth after his grid penalty.

QUALIFYING CLASSIFICATIONCan't wait for Sunday! 🤩#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/qqi8hPDcKA

“It is fantastic. We have been trying many grand prix to get pole. Sometimes a bit closer than others but to finally get it, from where we started the season, pretty incredible. I am happy with today and, for sure, I am going to try and win tomorrow. When you start first, that is the target.”

Big disappointment that for Russell. After his win in Baku, where he said he finally felt hooked up to the car, he was desperate to build the momentum. P8, four places behind Antonelli, was not what he would have had in mind. Has it all to do in the race tomorrow.

Excellent (though not unexpected) pole for Verstappen, and a very good P2 for Hamilton. Could be some fireworks on the front row tomorrow.

*Hadjar’s three-place grid penalty will drop him down to eighth place for the race tomorrow.

Neither of the Red Bulls can improve in the first sector but it is those behind them who need significant improvements. The two Ferraris are going along nicely at the start of their final flying laps. Hadjar is unable to improve despite a purple final sector. Verstappen then goes fastest in the final sector and improves his advantage at the top.

Hamilton meanwhile went fastest in the middle sector and goes second fastest overall. Piastri cannot improve but stays ahead of Russell.

Norris is the final man across the line but is only fast enough for P6. That means that Verstappen takes pole in Malaysia, which is the first time this season that Red Bull have taken pole position. Hamilton is second with Hadjar third, although the Frenchman has a five-place grid penalty.

MAX VERSTAPPEN TAKES POLE FOR THE BAHRAIN GRAND PRIX IN MALAYSIA!! 👊#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/NgtaCAZacL

The two Red Bulls, who are one and two at the moment, will be the first two drivers across the line on these final efforts.

The other nine drivers in Q3 are in the pits so young Antonelli has the track to himself as he sets his one and only flying lap of Q3. He is over four tenths down on Verstappen through the first sector and has plenty of work to do.

The championship leader sets a decent middle sector where he loses no more time to Verstappen. As it stands he would put himself third before the others do their final runs. He comes across the line in P3 but will have the likes of Hamilton, Piastri, Leclerc, Norris and Russell trying to surpass him.

Russell is the first across the line and sets a time of a 1:36.032. He does not last long at the top as he is immediately displaced by Hadjar, who is half a second quicker.

Hamilton then comes over the line in second, just ahead of his teammate Leclerc. Piastri puts himself between the two Ferraris.

What about Verstappen? The man who won here the last time we were in Malaysia continues his great form today and goes quickest by more than three tenths.

Antonelli now heads out and will have the track to himself really. This is going to be the championship leader’s only flying lap of Q3.

Russell is the first man to head out for his first flying lap in Q3. Antonelli has remained in the pits with just one new set of softs remaining. Verstappen, who right now feels like the favourite for pole, will be one of the last across the line in these first attempts of Q3.

The fight for pole position in Sepang begins now as the green light is on at the end of the pit lane to get Q3 going.

Antonelli, due to that lap time deletion in Q2, has just one new set of softs for Q3, which could prove costly in his attempts to try and take pole.

P12 the best qualifying result of the season for Alonso. It was only his second time in Q2 after Hungary (P16).

I should add, P14 was also Lance Stroll’s best qualifying result of the season. His first outing in Q2 this year.

11. Liam Lawson (Racing Bulls)12. Fernando Alonso (Aston Martin)13. Carlos Sainz (Williams)14. Lance Stroll (Aston Martin)15. Franco Colapinto (Alpine)16. Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls)

With grid penalties already on their way, neither Colapinto nor Lindblad set lap times in Q2.

Verstappen, Leclerc, Piastri, Norris, Hadjar and Russell all remain in the pits. A bit of a risk for Russell down in eighth but his time should be enough to get into Q3.

Lindblad, who will start tomorrow’s race at the back of the grid after penalties, gives his teammate Lawson a tow down the back straight and it works as Lawson just sneaks into the top ten.

Can Bortoleto get back ahead though of Lawson? Yes he can and he will take the final place in Q3. Lawson thought he might be through but the tow was not enough.

Lindblad, who's taking a grid penalty for Sunday's race, gave team mate Lawson a tow but it wasn't quite enough to send the Kiwi into Q3#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/IMlrqg4ENv

As the young Italian starts his flying lap, there is no-one else out on track so no traffic. He is a lot more cautious at turn six this time than last time, when he had his lap time deleted.

He has not set blistering first and second sector times but a purple final sector puts him into second and the Italian is safely into Q3.

Plenty of other drivers are now heading around the track for their final flying laps of Q2.

11. Lance Stroll (Aston Martin)12. Carlos Sainz (Williams)13. Kimi Antonelli (Mercedes)14. Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls)15. Franco Colapinto (Alpine)16. Fernando Alonso (Aston Martin)

Mercedes have put a brand new set of softs onto Antonelli’s car as he heads out promptly, with no lap time to his name so far. Antonelli is still disputing the lap deletion over team radio but his team tell him the images show he exceeded track limits. This is now a lot of pressure on the championship leader; any mistake now and he will not make Q3. His teammate Russell is only in seventh.

Antonelli was fourth fastest but has had his lap time deleted for exceeding track limits at turn six. That is a big moment in Q2 and could prove problematic if he gets into Q3. Antonelli appeared to be confused when he was told about his lap deletion over team radio but the on-board view looked pretty clear-cut.

Piastri then comes across the line in third.

Here's the moment Kimi ran wide 👀#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/E0VdWdBt8x

The Dutchman looks in a great spot at the moment to take pole position today and his 1:35.696 is very quick. He is nearly four tenths quicker than Antonelli.

How about the Ferraris? Leclerc was quickest in the middle sector but is nearly three tenths down on Verstappen. Hamilton puts himself into third place. Russell is more than half a second down on Verstappen.

Verstappen has been shown a black and white flag for driving unnecessarily slowly. I doubt he will get a grid penalty for that but it will be a warning for the Dutchman.

Anyway, the drivers, other than Colapinto and Alonso, are on flying laps, with Verstappen currently fastest inthe first sector.

The green light is showing at the end of the pit lane and the second part of qualifying is under way. Like the start of Q1, it is hardly a stampede to go out.

17. Nico Hulkenberg (Audi)18. Oliver Bearman (Haas)19. Esteban Ocon (Haas)20. Alex Albon (Williams)21. Valtteri Bottas (Cadillac)22. Sergio Perez (Cadillac)

The Aston Martin of Stroll improves significantly from 20th and is set to make Q2, as is his teammate Alonso. A bit of a surprise to see the Aston Martins improve and make it into Q2.

Go Fernando! 🤩 Go Lance! 🤩First double Q2 appearance this season 🙌#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/xjiWYv6ycr

That has seen the Audi of Hulkenberg drop into the drop zone and the German is out. For contrast, his teammate improves to go into eighth place! Hulkenberg had a big lock up into turn 14, which proved very costly.

As it stands, eight of the top nine are remaining in the garage. Russell is in ninth and has not gone out but Gasly above him in eighth has. You would imagine Russell is perfectly safe.

17. Esteban Ocon (Haas)18. Alex Albon (Williams)19. Oliver Bearman (Haas)20. Lance Stroll (Aston Martin)21. Valtteri Bottas (Cadillac)22. Sergio Perez (Cadillac)

Ocon, in 17th, is quite far off Hulkenberg in 16th and needs more than four tenths to usurp him.

The screens in the media centre here in Sepang tell me that the air temp right now is 32.8C and the track temp is 58C. It feels even hotter. Lots of chat about cooling vests this week, which are optional. George Russell is among the drivers who isn’t using one, which is interesting a) because Russell has suffered badly from heat in the past (Qatar, Singapore) and b) because he says Mercedes chose to put the development money into car upgrades instead.

It’s an interesting admission. Not everyone is sold on the idea of cooling vests. Ferrari and McLaren will definitely be using them this weekend, for instance. Max Verstappen won’t as he doesn’t like them. Russell thinks the FIA should just develop the tech themselves and it shouldn’t be part of the budget cap.

“Our team have put a lot of emphasis this year on the cockpit temperature,” he said. “We won’t be running the cooling vest because we haven’t put the resource into making it robust enough. I feel we need the FIA just to step in and say ‘Here’s some money extra in the cost cap or there’s an external company who’s going to develop it for everybody’. Because we should all be wearing it. When it works, it works great. So, I would like to wear it this week, and I would like to wear it next week. But the team asked me...look, we can develop it, and we can put the money towards it...[but at a cost].

He added: “The top itself is not expensive ..you’ve got to effectively make a system where you can fit a block of dry ice or actual ice, and then has the airflow to circulate the cool water throughout. If that system isn’t robust enough, then suddenly you have no circulation, and then you get hot. You get ambient temperature circulating. The vest is one-design, but the system that circulates the water is different [at different teams].”

The two Ferraris are on medium tyres but Leclerc still puts himself into second place. He is then displaced by Hamilton, who slots in behind Verstappen. Good times from the Ferraris on the mediums.

What about the McLarens? Norris goes sixth fastest but is more than six tenths down on Verstappen. Then comes Piastri, who goes fourth fastest, just under four tenths off Verstappen.

Arguably the three favourites for pole; Antonelli, Russell and Verstappen, are all on flying laps.

The first sector goes the way of Verstappen, who is purple, and then the Dutchman goes purple in the middle sector.

Antonelli is two tenths faster than his teammate Russell but Verstappen is over half a second quicker than the Mercedes. Hadjar is then second fastest to show the pace in the Red Bull this weekend.

Most of the teams waited and waited to come out and then suddenly lots of drivers are sent out, resulting in a queue in the pits! With the high track temperatures and high degradation, the drivers are crawling around on their out laps to preserve these soft tyres.

Bumper to bumper in the pit lane! #F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/ff8JO9kB1g

The two Haas drivers have a free track to themselves whilst everyone else bides their time. In theory, as the hour of qualifying goes on, the track temperature should decrease and the more rubber that is laid down the faster the track should get.

Finally, just before the two Haas drivers finish their first flying laps, the rest of the grid is starting to emerge, led by the Mercedes duo.

The green light is showing at the end of the pit lane and Q1 is officially under way. The two Haas drivers are the first to head out. Other than that, it is a quiet start to Q1.

The top four teams; Mercedes, Red Bull, Ferrari and McLaren, all have a genuine chance of taking pole in Sepang today. I think the true favourites though have to be the Mercedes duo and Max Verstappen but with how close it between all four of the teams you cannot rule anything out.

It is 33 degrees celsius air temperature, with the track temperature up at 58 degrees.

Not long to wait now until qualifying begins. It is hot, humid and dry in Sepang right now. As we know in Malaysia, the weather can change quickly and thunderstorms can roll in quite quickly but it looks like today’s qualifying will be a dry one. This will be one of if not the hottest qualifying sessions of the season, so much so that we are seeing umbrellas going up to get some shade from the sun rather than sheltering from any rain.

This will be important to consider after qualifying finishes as there will be some shuffling around:

Isack Hadjar (Red Bull): five-place grid penalty- new internal combustion engineFranco Colapinto (Alpine): ten-place grid penalty- new engineFranco Colapinto (Alpine): five-place grid penalty- causing a collision in BakuArvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls): back of the grid- complete power unit change

Hadjar has looked good since returning from his wrist injury so could be fighting it out near the front of the grid, although his five-place penalty will drop him down. We know Lindblad will be at the back and is very likely to be joined there by Colapinto, who is not going to be qualifying high up in the top ten in his Alpine.

Haas have announced that Frenchman Esteban Ocon will leave at the end of this season. Ocon now faces an uncertain future, with it difficult to see a spot for him on the F1 grid next season. There are suggestions that the 30-year-old’s replacement will be Brazilian Ferrari junior Rafael Camara, although nothing has been confirmed on that front. 21-year-old Camara currently leads the Formula 2 championship.

TGR Haas F1 Team and Esteban Ocon will part ways at the conclusion of the 2026 season. With plenty of racing ahead, our focus remains on working together to maximize every opportunity through to the final race of the year.#HaasF1 #F1 pic.twitter.com/4iQAuqnSyA

Aston Martin have now confirmed their driver line-up for next season, retaining both Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll. There had been reports that Alonso had been contemplating retirement but the 45-year-old will continue into another season.

Aston Martin Aramco confirms Lance and Fernando will continue as the team's drivers in 2027. Read more: ​https://t.co/ePyjJdyAIB pic.twitter.com/VogFUEbNxy

Other than the second seat alongside Ollie Bearman at Haas, the only other team to keep an eye on is Racing Bulls, with no definite confirmation on their exact driver line-up for next season.

Ferrari this week have publicly backed their team principal Frederic Vasseur, amid speculation over the Frenchman’s position and comments made by former Red Bull team principal Christian Horner, who said the job at Ferrari would be a “dream job”. Ferrari, who sit second in the constructors’ standings, have not won the drivers’ championship since 2007 (Kimi Raikkonen) and the constructors’ since 2008. Here is a snippet from Tom Cary’s piece on the matter:

In a hastily convened media call on Tuesday morning, Maria Conti, Ferrari’s chief communication officer, said the Scuderia had decided to issue a vote of confidence in Vasseur in response “not just to the story of Mr Horner, but in general, the speculation about Fred”.

“Ferrari has made its choices,” Conti said. “We have confidence – full confidence – in Fred Vasseur and in his team, and we continue to do so.

“At this time, it’s really important that the team remains united and cohesive, and we are focused with all the energy on the work ahead.”

“It is great to be back [in Malaysia]. I am really enjoying the track. We have had some wonderful races here over time. It is actually the 20th time we have been here, it started in 1999, and it is really exciting to be back. I really enjoyed getting out on the track and watching the cars closely.

“The drivers are super fit and they have some cooling but it is not easy. But you almost cannot get enough fluid through your body before your stomach gives up. Having this race and Singapore back-to-back increases that challenge.”

Especially with the big upgrade they have brought this weekend, Mercedes’ lead at the summit is looking unassailable right now.

Almost nine years ago to the day, Max Verstappen took just his second race victory in Formula 1. Lewis Hamilton, who took pole position, and Daniel Ricciardo joined Verstappen on the podium. Despite being nine years ago, plenty of drivers still on the grid were racing that weekend. Here they are and who they were racing for:

Max Verstappen (Red Bull) Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes) Valtteri Bottas (Mercedes) Esteban Ocon (Force India)Nico Hulkenberg (Renault)Sergio Perez (Force India)Fernando Alonso (McLaren)Lance Stroll (Williams)Carlos Sainz (Toro Rosso)Pierre Gasly (Toro Rosso)

With Russell winning in Baku and Antonelli finishing fifth, the latter’s championship lead was cut to 66 points. If Russell is going to usurp his teammate, he is going to need a few more similar results to last weekend due to the size of Antonelli’s lead. If Antonelli were to suffer a retirement, then that completely changes the outlook.

Formula One returns to Malaysia for round 16 of the season for the Bahrain Grand Prix. That probably sounds strange but after the Bahrain Grand Prix was originally postponed in March, F1 reinstated it to the calendar with Malaysia hosting it because of the ongoing war in the Middle East. Despite being held in Malaysia, Bahrain have retained the naming rights for the event, which is officially known as the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. The last time Formula One was in Malaysia was nine years ago back in 2017, when a young whippersnapper named Max Verstappen, still four years away from winning his first world championship, claimed just his second victory.

Last time out around the streets of Baku, Mercedes’ George Russell claimed victory at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, pipping Verstappen by just a tenth of a second. That was Russell’s first grand prix win since June and cuts his team-mate Kimi Antonelli’s lead in the drivers’ standings to 66 points. Antonelli had a challenging weekend in Baku, starting 16th after a crash in qualifying and coming home in fifth to see his championship lead to Russell cut by 15 points.

Verstappen was quickest in first practice yesterday, with the Ferrari of Charles Leclerc fastest in second practice. Earlier today, championship leader Antonelli was nearly three tenths clear of the field in third practice. Mercedes, 160 points clear at the top of the constructors’ standings, have brought significant upgrades this weekend, which includes a new floor, rear suspension and rear corner. It is the team’s first significant car update since the Canadian Grand at the end of May.

This race in Malaysia represents the second leg of the season’s first flyaway triple header, with the Singapore Grand Prix to come next weekend, so the demands on the teams and the drivers are incredibly high. Qualifying from Sepang gets under way at 9am (GMT).

#1453. Didier Deschamps 'doesn't want Manchester United job': Blow for Sir Jim Ratcliffe as unemployed former France boss appears hesitant to replace under-fire Michael Carrick

Published: 04:37 EDT, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 04:37 EDT, 6 November 2026

Manchester United have suffered a road bump in sounding out potential replacements for Michael Carrick – as Didier Deschamps reportedly doesn't want the gig.

Deschamps, who left the France job after 14 years following the World Cup, has told the club he is uninterested according to the Daily Mirror.

Carrick remains in post but his bosses have been privately talking to possible successors for weeks after an abysmal start to the season which has left them 17th in the Premier League.

Eddie Howe, Fabian Hurzeler, Unai Emery and Antonio Conte have all come up on the shortlist, with the international break this month seen as an ideal time for managerial changes across the league.

Deschamps appealed to United because of his immediate availability and lack of a compensation fee, but is in no rush to take a job and snubbed their advance.

After a glittering career as a player, he has won the World Cup managing France, lifted Ligue 1 with Marseille, led Monaco to a Champions League final, and got Juventus promoted back to Serie A after the Calciopoli scandal.

Didier Deschamps has reportedly told Manchester United he is not interested in the job

Michael Carrick remains in post but United have been sounding out potential replacements for weeks

Carrick's prospects of keeping the job had a boost on Tuesday as Matheus Cunha struck two late goals to produce a stunning turnaround win against Roma in the Champions League.

But he only has a clash against Aston Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday afternoon before the international break to prove to the hierarchy that he should keep his job.

That comeback against Roma stopped a rot which has been spreading for weeks. United were on the verge of going ten games without a win, a run unprecedented in the club's history.

They have reached a nadir in recent weeks after batterings by Como and Bournemouth – the latter at Old Trafford, no less – while players have been openly mutinous.

Bruno Fernandes publicly criticised Carrick's tactics after the 4-1 defeat at Como, leading to Carrick benching him for the next game against Bournemouth.

And Lisandro Martinez has singled out director of football Jason Wilcox over United's transfer activity, suggesting the squad was left short on quality after the transfer window.

Were Carrick to go, it is unclear who would replace him.

Emery is open to signing a new deal with Aston Villa which would take him to close to a decade at the club, and held a meeting with club chiefs on Wednesday.

Hurzeler does not have a release clause in his Brighton contract and so would require enormous compensation. There is well-placed scepticism as to whether any move would even be remotely possible, regardless of how well liked he is inside Old Trafford.

Nagelsmann and Conte are both out of work and the latter has previously indicated that he would like the challenge of restoring a fallen giant to glory.

#1452. 'Why are you speaking? F*** off!': Kevin De Bruyne at centre of Napoli dressing room meltdown as 'divided' squad lurches towards 'disaster'... with an 'every man for himself' culture setting in at Italian giants

Published: 03:23 EDT, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 05:08 EDT, 6 November 2026

Kevin De Bruyne was told to 'f*** off' repeatedly during Napoli's 4-1 thrashing against Porto on Wednesday, with a dressing room crisis heating up at the club.

The Napoli squad has become increasingly fractured in recent weeks, according to the Italian media, with an 'every man for himself' culture developing into a 'disaster'.

Napoli sit eighth in Serie A under new manager Massimiliano Allegri – just two seasons after winning the title under Antonio Conte – and are near the bottom of the Champions League table after three defeats in four games.

Their cracks are showing on the pitch, with striker Lorenzo Lucca yelling at De Bruyne: 'Why are you speaking? F*** off!' during their Porto drubbing.

The pair squared up to each other and Lucca shouted his expletive command three times before they went their separate ways.

After the match, Matteo Politano told Sky Sport Italia: 'It would be nice if a few other teammates came here to give an explanation and not just us Italians, but never mind, I never hide my face.'

Kevin De Bruyne was told to 'f*** off' three times by team-mate Lorenzo Lucca during Napoli's 4-1 defeat by Porto on Wednesday

There is said to be a rift developing between Napoli's native stars and foreign players

La Gazzetta dello Sport reported that Politano was calling out Cameroonian star Frank Anguissa and Kosovan Amir Rrahmani, both two-time title winners with the club.

Politano added: 'The attitude is one that a team like ours cannot have at this level. I was not attacking anyone, we have a squad that is struggling, but we need to come together and think about this next game before the break for international duty.

'Hopefully we can recover a few players during that spell and then our season can really begin.'

There is a 'divide' between the Italian group of players and foreigners, La Gazzetta dello Sport reports, though it is mostly down to frustration with results.

Individuals such as De Bruyne, Rasmus Hojlund, and Stanislav Lobotka are more 'reserved personalities' who have reportedly not bonded as well with their team-mates away from the field.

Scott McTominay, who has an ally in fellow Scottish player Billy Gilmour, said after the Porto loss: 'Of course I’m angry.

'We lost 4-1 in the Champions League; there’s nothing to smile about. For us, it’s go on and try to figure out how to fix it.

'We’ve had a lot of injuries, a lot of important players you can’t change; attacking players as well. Let’s not beat around the bush; we’ve got a lot of injuries, and that makes a big difference whenever you come into play every three days.

Napoli have had a rough start to the season under new manager Massimiliano Allegri - despite him being a legendary coach in Italy

'So, things like these can make a huge difference for the team when the same players are playing over and over again. People need to understand that, but we also need to do better. First and foremost, we need to do better, injuries in football are part of it, but we have too many.'

Their dressing room troubles have dragged on for a while. Last season, Conte complained of a lack of unity after they signed nine players on the back of their Scudetto. They still managed to finish second, but it was a turbulent ride.

'Nine new players were too many. We weren't balanced,' he said at the time.

'I experience the dressing room every day, so I say certain things; we mustn't despair. We'll try to recreate last year's chemistry.'

In one match against AC Milan, De Bruyne threw a tantrum after being subbed off by Conte.

#1451. An open structure-guided RNA foundation model for generalizable prediction

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

RNA language models have achieved strong performance across diverse downstream tasks by leveraging large-scale sequence data. However, RNA function is fundamentally shaped by hierarchical structure, making structural information important for pre-training. Existing approaches often depend on noisy annotations or task-specific objectives that can limit generalizability. Here we present structRFM, a structure-guided RNA foundation model trained on 21 million RNA sequence–structure pairs by integrating base-pairing interactions into masked language modelling through a pair-matching operation. We also introduce MUSES, a multi-source ensemble of secondary structures designed to mitigate predictor bias, and a dynamic masking ratio that balances structure-guided and nucleotide-level masking. structRFM learns joint sequence and structure representations as sequence-level, nucleotide-level and pairwise features for broad downstream adaptation. It ranks highly in zero-shot homology classification and establishes new benchmarks for secondary-structure prediction. Its tertiary-structure adaptation, Zfold, consistently improves both three-dimensional predictions and their extracted secondary structures, with performance comparable to AlphaFold31 across CASP15-natural, CASP16 and RNA-Puzzles. structRFM also improves performance on function-prediction tasks and generalizes to newly released RNA families and long non-coding RNAs. Together, these results demonstrate the effectiveness of structure-guided pre-training and highlight multimodal RNA language models for robust structural and functional inference. The complete 21-million-pair dataset, model weights and source code are openly available to support multimodal RNA foundation-model development.

The training and test datasets are publicly available at GitHub (https://github.com/heqin-zhu/structRFM), which are from the following sources: RNAcentral v24.041: https://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/RNAcentral/releases/24.0/; Rfam v14.1066,67: https://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/Rfam/14.10/and Rfam v15.0: https://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/Rfam/15.0/; ArchiveII600 and ArchiveII37: https://rna.urmc.rochester.edu/publications.html; RNAStrAlign35: https://github.com/mxfold/mxfold2/releases/tag/v0.1.0; bpRNA-1m, bpRNA-TR0 and bpRNA-TS036: https://bprna.cgrb.oregonstate.edu/download.php#bpRNA; PDB46,47: https://www.rcsb.org/; CASP1527: https://predictioncenter.org/download_area/CASP15; CASP1628: https://predictioncenter.org/download_area/CASP16; RNA-Puzzles48: https://www.rnapuzzles.org/puzzles/list/; SpliceAI4: https://github.com/Illumina/SpliceAI; IRES29,30: Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) accessions GSE74277 and GSE178718; nRC31: http://tblab.pa.icar.cnr.it/public/nRC/paper_dataset/; lncRNA-Human (GENCODE 2021)56: https://www.gencodegenes.org/human/; lncRNA-Mouse (GENCODE 2021)56: https://www.gencodegenes.org/mouse/; and the NCBI nucleotide (nt) database42: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/blast/db/. The study-specific processed IRES split and source data underlying the figures are provided with this paper. All other data are available within the article and its Supplementary Information. No restrictions apply. Source data are provided with this paper.

The source code of structRFM is publicly available at Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18274292 (ref. 78)) and GitHub (https://github.com/heqin-zhu/structRFM).

a Ternary simplex visualization of the MUSES performance landscape across weighted combination configurations. Each vertex corresponds to a single standalone method (BPfold, ViennaRNA or CONTRAfold), and interior points represent weighted ensemble models. We normalized weighting coefficients for proportional equivalence and applied linear interpolation over a dense grid to smooth the INF metric distribution. Colour gradients (blue to red) represent INF values, with contour lines for enhanced resolution. This visualization illustrates how ensemble weighting modulates MUSES performance for robust secondary-structure annotation and identifies optimal weight-coefficient regimes with associated trade-offs. b Benchmark evaluation of six established multi-source RNA secondary-structure prediction methods23,24,25,26,34,44,45,79 on the Rfam66,67 and full ArchiveII37 (n = 3, 975 independent RNA sequences) datasets, stratified by three sequence-length categories (≤ 500 nt, 501–1000 nt, > 1000 nt). c Linear fits extrapolating prediction performance for the six methods on both datasets. Lines are linear regression fits, and shaded bands represent 95% confidence intervals. A substantial performance degradation is observed with increasing sequence length, highlighting the current challenge of modelling RNA secondary structures for long RNA sequences.

a Head-to-head comparison of structRFM with other models using ϵRMSD72, TM-score73, GDT-TS74 and INF75. Circle size indicates the absolute difference between the two methods. b Violin plots of RMSD values. For each method in b, n = 8 independent RNA targets for CASP15-natural, n = 13 independent RNA targets for CASP16, and n = 20 independent RNA targets for RNA-Puzzles. The inner box plots show the median (white centre line), 25th and 75th percentiles (lower and upper bounds of the thick line), and minimum and maximum (lower and upper thin whiskers).

The ϵRMSD, TM-score and GDT-TS of tertiary structures, together with the INF of secondary structures extracted from tertiary structures, are annotated. In the secondary-structure diagrams, stems are shown in green, multiple loops in red, interior loops in yellow, hairpin loops in blue, and 5′ and 3′ unpaired regions in orange. In general, structRFM performs better on natural targets than on synthetic targets containing dense long-range interactions, but sometimes fails to predict short local stems (in green), resulting in large multiple loops (in red).

The ϵRMSD, TM-score and GDT-TS of tertiary structures, together with the INF of secondary structures extracted from tertiary structures, are annotated. In the secondary-structure diagrams, stems are shown in green, multiple loops in red, interior loops in yellow, hairpin loops in blue, and 5’ and 3’ unpaired regions in orange. In general, structRFM performs better on viral and aptamer targets but performs worse on multimer and bacterial targets. For targets marked with blue circles, the sequences used for CASP16 prediction differ substantially from those of the PDB ground-truth structures because regions unresolved in the experimental structures were not modelled.

a Overall comparison of methods for IRES identification using seven metrics. b Overall comparison of methods for ncRNA classification using seven metrics. c PR and ROC curves for the 13 individual classes in the nRC dataset.

Canonical base pairs represent approximately half of all interactions, including GC (26.5%), AU (14.4%) and GU (7.2%) pairs. d Distribution of confidence scores for predicted secondary structures. Most predictions have high confidence scores, supporting the reliability of the base-pairing annotations.

#1450. Sublime England thrash Croatia in best performance for a decade

If this is Tuchel-ball, if this is the way Thomas Tuchel wants England to play, then yes, please. More of the same; bring it on. The standard is set.

England’s DNA? This was a total-football annihilation of a top nation. Croatia, 14th in the world and fierce competitors, were cowed and humiliated at home in this Nations League tie. This was the biggest defeat in their proud history – seventh heaven for England, and hell for the hosts.

The visitors were sublime. Harry Kane (twice – 89 goals now for his country), Jude Bellingham and Anthony Gordon all scored and were outstanding. Bukayo Saka also struck twice. Alex Scott made his first start and will take some dislodging. The Bournemouth midfielder was slick with a snap – perpetual, intelligent, smooth motion.

Harry Kane at the DOUBLE! 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿The Three Lions have FIVE in Rijeka 🦁 pic.twitter.com/BRnVXADtHC

Luka Modric has had the most extraordinary career but he was emphatically second best here and was subbed off on 57 minutes at 5-0. He looked bereft, having had Scott and Elliot Anderson run all over him and Mateo Kovacic.

We came out of the World Cup wondering if Tuchel really had an idea of how he can get England over the line. After last Saturday’s defeat by world and European champions Spain, followed by Tuesday’s win over the Czech Republic we still did not know.

But here the standard was set – it was an exhilarating example of the football England are capable of. On display we saw the speed, the movement, the passes under pressure, the ambition, the control and aggression. This was the full package. Bottle it. Bag it. Believe it.

Croatia have an ageing team and are in transition, but they were left looking callow. It looked as though it was men against boys. There were plenty of boys in the stands, with 6,200 children allowed in for what was supposed to be a behind-closed-doors fixture – Croatia’s punishment for crowd trouble.

Their new head coach Slaven Bilic would doubtless have been relieved that the match was not played in front of the usual, passionate, partisan crowd. Even then some of the kids booed and left early. Bilic looked shell-shocked. As well he might.

And Saka makes it FOUR! ⚽️⚽️⚽️⚽️England break to devastating effect - Croatia are reeling... pic.twitter.com/60EgNt4cfh

It was 4-0 at half-time. It could easily have been 7-1 – Kovacic missed a sitter for Croatia at 3-0 and Gordon should have had a hat-trick. How significant is it that England’s three most dangerous players do not play in the Premier League? Probably not very. But the fact they turn out for Real Madrid, Barcelona and Bayern Munich is. They performed like the top players their clubs think they clearly are.

Gordon heads in to make it THREE! 💥England are cruising 🛳️ pic.twitter.com/nqwUxFmkof

Kane’s commitment was incredible. At one stage Croatia substitute Kristijan Jakić threatened to break clear but was stopped by England’s last man tracking back. It was Kane, one cap short of equalling Peter Shilton’s all-time record of 125 appearances, and it was already 5-0 when that happened.

These could be exciting times for England. Times when they have shaken off the debate over how well or otherwise they did at the World Cup and moved on. Tuchel has talked up that third-place finish; we have tended to dwell on the semi-final exit to Argentina.

And now? If Tuchel does go and win a trophy for England, he will be talking about this game. Previously he referenced the 5-0 demolition of Serbia in Belgrade, during the World Cup qualification. But the Serbians were a rabble. Croatia are not, but were made to look so on Saturday.

Where will this sit among England performances? There was the 2-1 victory away to Italy at the beginning of the Euro 2024 qualification campaign in March 2023. Before that, the 3-2 win away to Spain in 2018, also in the Nations League. But England were more thrilling here. Do we have to go back to 5-1 in Munich in 2001?

The concern will be the familiar England problem of looking like world-beaters in the autumn and worn out by the time a tournament comes around in the summer. But against Croatia there was control and authority as they raised their chances of finishing in the top two and qualifying for next March’s quarter-finals.

The goals rained in – even if the best remained the first as Marc Guéhi intercepted a clearance, Scott took the ball on the half-turn and found Bellingham. He slid it through to Kane who finished high into the net. What a goal.

Bellingham ➡️ Kane! ⚽️The Three Lions lead in Rijeka with their first shot on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/ZLcnGLvj3z

England were swarming all over Croatia. Saka crossed, Gordon took the ball down and turned it back for Bellingham to stab home.

What a touch from Anthony Gordon! 🔥The Barca man squares it to the Real Madrid man and England lead 2-0 ⚽️⚽️ pic.twitter.com/31Y1Ojx44M

Gordon, after twice being denied, got his goal – with another header, as against the Czechs. This time Jarell Quansah, back in ahead of Trent Alexander-Arnold, delivered from the right and Gordon met it to score for the fourth successive game for England. Even before half-time England were not finished as Bellingham crossed low from the left and found Saka, who found the back of the net.

After the break, the hunger remained insatiable. Anderson was sent down the right and Kane slid in. Croatia then lost the ball sloppily inside their own area, Kane thought about shooting but unselfishly fed Saka, who claimed a second goal.

Saka should have had a hat-trick before substitute Morgan Rogers wrapped up the scoring, collecting a ball over the top from the relentless Bellingham – once again captain after Kane went off – and finishing with ease after rounding the goalkeeper. It was a third assist for Bellingham and a seventh goal for England. It could have been double figures.

SEVENTH heaven for England! 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿Morgan Rogers is the latest player to put his name on the scoresheet... ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/H5txZRVgLC

Absolutely [that was the 90-minute performance we’ve been looking for]. Maybe three minutes after the three-zero there was a big mistake [Kovacic’s chance] and some easy ball losses but that was a performance of the highest level from everyone. And from the first until the last minute from everyone who started and everyone who came on. Congratulations to the team.

Very, very impressive [to do this] on an away pitch. We created so many chances in the first 40 minutes. We were so fluid from the start. I looked at the clock and thought ‘Oh, this has been a good three minutes, this has been a good seven minutes…’ and it never stopped.

We kept the pace up and played through the gaps, stayed hungry in our counter-pressing and defending.

We played humble and always got the basics right.

Unbelievable from start to finish. We spoke a lot about having a 90-minute game in which we were dominant with and without the ball and that was it out there. We’re at our best when we’re brave and we’re physically overpowering. When we make it a Premier League game and they couldn’t live with our pace, our movement, our runs. And we were clinical.

There’s freedom. All four of us [him, Bellingham, Saka and Gordon] can play in the 10 pocket, play as the nine. I can play as a midfielder. We’re good enough and smart enough so if we lose the ball we can cover in midfield and defence. That’s the way we want to play. It’s so hard for them to pick a man and press. Every man was at the highest level.

Beautiful hotel, lovely weather, we could easily have fallen into that holiday mode. It’s an unusual situation for us. We’ve never been away this long in this kind of camp and that’s the perfect end to the week,

[And now to equal Peter Shilton’s record 125th cap on Tuesday?] That would be nice. That’s why he keeps taking me off, to rest me for the next game. That’s what he said to me after. I’ll be ready to start on Tuesday.

An amazing night for us. We came out from the start on top and played with high energy and we punished them.

It was special and fun to play. We were really clinical today. Two goals for England is always a nice feeling.

We showed the hunger, passion and quality we had. A mixture of everything we wanted to show.

[Bellingham] was amazing tonight. He deserved man of the match and deserves to be player of the year.

At least the Croatia fans did not seem too dispirited, the kids smiling and waving at the camera, despite the utter trouncing their team took.

England were terrific but how much of that was because Croatia were terrible will be open to debate.

Eze just overcooks the pass that would have released Gibbs-White to run through on goal.

That was Bellingham’s third assist and should it stay 7-0 after two minutes of stoppage time, it will be Croatia’s heaviest defeat.

Nice line from the englandstats.com X account - who said you can’t win anything with kids… watching. Although quite a lot of them have now headed for the exits. This has been remarkable.

Croatia 0 England 7 (Rogers) He barely celebrates but it was a finish off the highest class. He bent his run to make Jakic play him onside, ran down the left when through one-on-one, feigned to cut in then rounded the keeper on the outside to shoot crisply into the open net as Livakovic, who has not been at fault all night, scrambled desperately.

SEVENTH heaven for England! 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿Morgan Rogers is the latest player to put his name on the scoresheet... ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/H5txZRVgLC

Rogers is fouled but not before he pings a pass out to Saka on the right. The Arsenal winger darts at Perisic then fizzes a pass across the box to Bellingham who almost trips over himself when block-tackled.

Quansah blocks Perisic’s cross and Croatia want a penalty for Konsa’s tackle on Ivanovic. Looked OK to me and the referee.

Lewis-Skelly → HallGibbs-White → Anderson.

So no Alexander-Arnold or Calvert-Lewin. I suspect he never really intends to give either a decent number of minutes unless forced by circumstances.

England are readying two more substitutes. England scored six against France only a couple of games ago, can they go one better? They put seven past North Macedonia in 2023 but Croatia are two levels above that side.

Bellingham and Eze are playing through the middle now with Rogers down the left.

England really ought to be in double figures by now.

Saka spurns a chance for his hat-trick at the back post when teed up with a Rogers cross from the left.

Croatia 0 England 6 (Saka) Frankly ridiculous. Stanisic, in the right-back position, chips the ball with his left foot across the penalty area straight to Saka who chests it down, plays a one-two with Kane and then buries a right-foot shot past the utterly exposed Livakovic. I know Stanisic and Kane are team-mates at Bayern but that is taking comradely generosity to preposterous extremes.

It's a GIFT for England! 🎁🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿Bukayo Saka has his second... The Three Lions are relentless. pic.twitter.com/33a8oxd3be

Gordon hares down the left at full pelt, the ball seemingly velcroed to his left foot as he makes the byline and cuts the ball back looking for Kane. Vuskovic makes the first block that rebounds to the winger and Gvardiol the second.

Kane’s wandering is often a source of frustration but he has been superb tonight even if he has been allowed to run free.

Pickford catches the corner at his front post. England go forward, pulling defence and midfield one way and then the other with their incisive passing.

Croatia have a corner. Matanovic’s shot from 20 yards takes a deflection and dribbles wide.

Vuskovic has been very impressive for Brighton and Guradiola felt Gvardiol was worth his weight in gold. They have been rubbish tonight.

Bellingham now has the chance of doubling up when Pasalic carelessly loses the ball and turns in horror to see Gordon striding away with it. The Barcelona winger looks for Bellingham and finds him with a cute pass down the inside left. Bellingham stops in the hope Livakovic will go down but when he tries to dink it over him he skews it past the right post.

Croatia 0 England 5 (Kane) That brief revival of Croatia’s press dies a death as England waltz through the midfield again and Anderson drives into the box down the right and bends a cross around the retreating centre-backs to the back post. Kane slides in to prod it home, telescoping out his right leg to convert with the outside of his boot.

Harry Kane at the DOUBLE! 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿The Three Lions have FIVE in Rijeka 🦁 pic.twitter.com/BRnVXADtHC

Bellingham pings a diagonal out to Gordon who dribbles into the box down the left, executes a step-over to gull the right-back and then cuts the ball into the six-yard box. Gvardiol wellies it away from Bellingham.

England sweep the ball around confidently with Kane sitting deep and spraying some passes out to the wings with precision.

Ivanovic times the press perfectly with Modric to dispossess  Saka and then slip the ball ahead to Mantanovic and the Freiburg forward tries to catch Pickford napping with an early shot from 30 yards that whistles past the left post. It did give Pickford the hurry-up.

Matanovic is penalised for a foul on Konsa which didn’t look like a foul to me.

The young crowd’s verve has been thoroughly doused by that first-half performance and you can hear the England fans at the start of the half as Croatia kick off.

Matanovic → MusaVlasic → BaturinaMario Pasalic → Sucic

“He’s like a grown man playing against children, giving them a pat on the head as he goes past them.”

England have been magnificent going forward and with their press. Croatia have been shambolic. Bilic lasted six years in his first stint in the job. He’ll be lucky to last six months in this spell if this is the level of his players’ commitment.

Racking my brains to recall the last time England played this well against a leading nation, against any nation in fact. Maybe it was the 3-2 win away over Spain, again in the Nations League in 2018?

Croatia 0 England 4 (Saka) It’s as if Croatia have thrown in the towel. They let Gordon run in behind again on the left and pass to Bellingham who faces up Modric, jinks to his left, shimmies with a wiggle of the shoulder to beat him down the side and then centre to Saka who taps it in, left alone by the negligent Vuskovic and Gvardiol.

And Saka makes it FOUR! ⚽️⚽️⚽️⚽️England break to devastating effect - Croatia are reeling... pic.twitter.com/60EgNt4cfh

Blimey! Kovacic has just missed an open goal as he exploited a lack of concentration at the back by Anderson to blindside him and take the ball off him to dribble to his right through the box with Pickford scrambling like crazy. Once he had opened up the gap to shoot through from the right of the penalty spot, he speared it inches wide. The crowd could not be more deflated if you poked them with a hat-pin.

A STUNNING miss from Mateo Kovačić 🫣The Man City man rounds the keeper and misses an open goal. pic.twitter.com/YfPuDehwYf

I wonder if Luka Modric has ever been in the position where he has not been the best player on the pitch in a headband? Well tonight he’s not, as Alex Scott has been excellent on his first England start. He’s pressed high, dropped deep, won the ball back, beaten his man. It’s just amazing it’s taken Tuchel this long to start him.

I think a few of us (me included) might have thought Trent Alexander-Arnold was the only England full-back who could have provided the cross for Gordon to score against the Czech Republic. Well we were wrong, as Quansah produced a carbon copy of Trent’s cross for Gordon to score with his head against Croatia. Who knew he had that in his locker?

Croatia 0 England 3 (Gordon) His goal on Tuesday was a very rare header and now he’s added a second. Kane sent Quansah down the right and the right-back whipped over a cross that Gordon allowed to bounce in front of him and then flopped rather than dived forward to bury at the back post. He’s the new Nat Lofthouse.

Gordon heads in to make it THREE! 💥England are cruising 🛳️ pic.twitter.com/nqwUxFmkof

A spell of possession beyond 30 seconds for Croatia for the first time. Scott is in the right place to intercept and scupper the first thrust and then Pickford comes a long way off his line and has a bit of a flap at a cross but gets enough of his fist on it, even if he misjudged the flight, to get away with it.

Bilic has sent his outfield subs to warm up. Might be some damage limitation imminent. Modric, if he is to play, ought to be as a 10 not in this deep role.

The young locals are growing restless now. Bood greeted England’s second goal and it felt they were directed at Croatia, rather than the England team. England’s 100-strong band of supporters are making themselves heard and are witnessing an excellent performance so far.

Thomas Tuchel could not believe Anthony Gordon did not kill the game from Bellingham’s cross. He turned to the bench when the ball did not hit the back of the net and angrily remonstrated about the fact England had not scored. He wants this game done and dusted while his team are so dominant.

The tide is relentless. Konsa miscues Saka’s cross from a  free-kick behind for a goal-kick and moments later Anderson, flooding into acres of vacated space, blazes over from 20 yards.

England are playing with the fluency and swagger of a side that are 5-0 up. In fact they could well have been. Kane’s goal was his 88th for England. Bellingham’s his 14th.

Bellingham quickly returns the favour to Gordon with a brilliant run down the right. Gordon checks his run then bends it past Vuskovic’s shoulder to receive the curling cross but he clips it from six yards straight into Livakovic’s chest as the goalkeeper spread himself starfish style.

Croatia 0 England 2 (Bellingham) A Clásico goal. Saka’s cross from the right, looking for Kane again, is overhit. But Gordon is there to trap it on the volley, take it down then slip a clever pass to Bellingham who pokes it past Livakovic. England are off to a flyer. Barcelona assist → Real Madrid finish.

What a touch from Anthony Gordon! 🔥The Barca man squares it to the Real Madrid man and England lead 2-0 ⚽️⚽️ pic.twitter.com/31Y1Ojx44M

England tear a hole through the heart of the Croatia defence again. Modric and Kovacic are just being swamped. Gordon, who was on the underlap as Hall brought it forward, pings the pass from the middle out to Saka who faces up Perisic and whips an inswinging cross with his left to the back post that Vuskovic juts gets to before Kane to glance it behind.

This is seriously the best I have seen England move the ball in a very long time. Their passing is slick and quick and they are so dangerous. Alex Scott is making a real difference in midfield. Feels strange it has taken Thomas Tuchel until now to start him but he is making a real impression and played a clever part in Harry Kane’s excellent team goal.

Another heart-in-mouth moment for the Croatia defence when Kane, drifting out to the right, arrows in the perfect cross that sits up nicely for Saka to toe towards goal from close range. It dribbles past the post and the flag goes up to spare his recriminations.

England have started this game brilliantly, but Croatia have been woeful. They’ve barely strung a pass together and should be two goals down already.

England almost make it two in two minutes when their high press, vigorously applied, forces another error and allows Anderson tos end Gordon racing behind Stanisic down the left. Saka keeps pace with him through the middle but Gordon, in the form of his life, is never going to lay it off and hammers a shot instead that Livakovic turns away.

And that is exactly why it pays to warm-up seriously. Kane was lethal in the pre-match warm-up, see my earlier post, and finished his first chance in the game superbly. Practice makes perfect.

Croatia 0 England 1 (Kane) Gvardiol brings the ball out of the area to the left then sprays a pass into the centre-circle that his City team-mate, Guehi, intercepts. Guehi passes it to Scott who shifts it quickly upfield to Bellingham and the No10 slips a delightful reverse pass between the left-back and centre-half into Kane’s path. The England captain calmly lifts his shot over Livakovic and high into the net.

Bellingham ➡️ Kane! ⚽️The Three Lions lead in Rijeka with their first shot on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/ZLcnGLvj3z

Sucic is penalised for a sliding tackle on Bellingham that legs up the England forward in full flight down the left. Saka takes it, crossing on a shallow arc to the 18-yard line. Guéhi cushions a header but too close to a defender for Kane to pounce.

Anderson takes the corner short and Croatia defend the belated cross.

Looks like the Croatian kids were busy in art and English classed this week, as they unfurled a banner that read ‘It’s not coming home’ in one side of the ground as the game kicked off.

England attack up the left patiently, turning back when necessary. Kane drops deep and fires a pass to Bellingham who plays it down the inside-left for Gordon who runs beyond Vuskovic and rakes a left-foot shot that Livakovic, his Cam Nou team-mate, turns behind.

Alex Scott is given the first kick of the game, knocks it all the way back to Pickford who pumps it so long that Livakovic comes for it and makes a mess of it, shanking it out for a throw-in.

The Croatia national anthem is belted out. Croatia are heart-clutchers when they sing their anthem. It seems an increasingly common practice.

And it does sound like a schoolboy international. England are in red shirts and navy shorts, Croatia in their white and red chequerboard.

You can hear the players singing the national anthem.

Three sides of the ground are now full of small children – and some bigger children who look suspiciously like adults. There’s every chance that I either end this game with a headache or running away from a pack of dogs, given the high-pitched home support.

I just watched Anthony Barry put on a finishing drill with some of the England players. The standard was pretty high, but the quality of Kane’s finishing was, unsurprisingly, superb. He scored with seven of his eight shots past James Trafford and Jason Steele. The one shot he didn’t score with forced Steele into an excellent save. You often see players go through the motions in the pre-match warm-up, but not Kane. He hit every shot like he was trying to win the game in the 90th minute. England’s starters have now gone in ahead of kick-off.

[The camp] has been very good, helped us unwind and recharge the batteries after two intense matches. We have been on the road for a few days, the setting was beautiful. Now we need to switch on which is very difficult [because] the atmosphere is very different with 6,000 children in the stadium. We want to make it a really competitive game but the surrounding is very different. I think wee are up for it.

[Alex Scott] did so well in training and did so well when he made his debut so he brings the full package. He has legs, good at defending, good in the high press, smooth on the ball and good decision-making. That is why he has our trust.

It was a close decision [over Alexander-Arnold] but we decided for Jarrell to start. We will have a lot to defend especially on that side with Perisic and Jarrell did well with Bukayo. We have Trent as an option from the bench.

We need a complete performance in all aspects, adapt to the circumstances. Our physicality, if it is a real competitive match then we would have the edge. Now it feels more like an open training session with the environment and that will suit them better.

But I hope we can bring the intensity and then have the edge.

"To be fair, I don't care" 🤷‍♂️😂Never change, Slaven Bilić 🇭🇷 pic.twitter.com/hBrtZ5TiBy

Loud (high-pitched) cheers for the Croatia team from children inside the Rijeka Stadium. Luka Modric, aged 41, is starting for the home team. He’s a year older than Wayne Rooney, who retired from international football nine years ago. The England players were booed when they entered the pitch. These kids know what they are doing.

I was here eight years ago when it really was a behind-closed-doors game for England. This is very different. There are around 6,000 Croatian children, with their guardians, here and the stands are filling up. It’s also pretty noisy with all the pre-match music.

In 2018, we could hear exactly what the managers and players were shouting – Jordan Henderson was particularly loud – but I don’t think that will be the case this time around. The noise from the fans may be quite high pitched today, but I don’t think it will be quiet at all.

England have 100 fans here and, mercifully, they have not been forced to watch from inside the metal caged away end. They haven’t been allowed to bring in England flags, so it’s currently quite hard to locate exactly where they are.

Croatia Livakovic; Stanisic, Vuskovic, Gvardiol, Perisic; Modric, Kovacic; Ivanovic, P Sucic, Baturina; Musa.Substitutes Pandur, Kotarski, Smolcic, Sutalo, Kramaric, Vlasic, Mario Pasalic, Jakic, Marco Pasalic, Matanovic, Luka Sucic, Misic.

England Pickford; Quansah, Konsa, Guéhi, Hall; Anderson, Scott; Saka, Bellingham, Gordon; Kane.Substitutes Trafford, Steele, Alexander-Arnold, Chalobah, Ngumoha, Branthwaite, Lewis-Skelly, Rogers, Garner, Calvert-Lewin, Gibbs-White, Eze.

Thomas Tuchel was glowing about Alex Scott in his pre-match media duties ahead of today’s game against Croatia and the midfielder has been handed his first England start.

Scott has come in for Myles Lewis-Skelly in what looks to be an attacking change from Tuchel, the England head coach.

Tuchel had taken Scott to the United States on his pre-World Cup training camp, but the Bournemouth midfielder was not part of the squad for the tournament-proper.

On Scott, Tuchel said: “I am super impressed by Alex Scott, I think he is at the moment one of the best central midfielders in the Premier League and he just proves it in every training session. He had a fantastic debut the other day and really really impressed me.”

🇭🇷🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 Croatia's starting XI vs. England!Petar Musa and Martin Baturina get their first starts under Slaven Bilić! pic.twitter.com/dPt32fiXbh

Your #ThreeLions for Saturday night 🔴🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 pic.twitter.com/A2M4lMfBNj

Jordan Pickford has revealed he spends up to three hours talking to a “mindwork coach”.

The England goalkeeper has worked with sports psychologists for some time but has gone into detail about how committed he is as he faces a challenge to his No 1 spot from James Trafford.

Pickford will start for England in the Nations League tie against Croatia, and next Tuesday’s fixture at home to the Czech Republic, having missed out on the past two games.

Trafford was in goal for the 3-2 loss to Spain and the 2-0 victory away to the Czechs and although Thomas Tuchel has said Pickford remains his first choice it is known that he and his coaching staff are huge admirers of Leeds United’s new goalkeeper.

Trent Alexander-Arnold is expected to drop back down to the substitutes’ bench for England’s third Nations League game against Croatia in Rijeka.

Despite Alexander-Arnold providing an assist for Anthony Gordon against the Czech Republic, England head coach Thomas Tuchel is expected to replace him with Jarell Quansah at right-back.

Jude Bellingham is also in line for a recall, most likely in place of Morgan Rogers, while Tuchel had been hopeful of Ezri Konsa returning to fitness to replace Trevoh Chalobah in the centre of defence. Goalkeeper Jordan Pickford replaces James Trafford.

Uefa fined the Croatian football federation £80,000 and ordered them to play their next Uefa-sanctioned home match behind closed doors because of their fans’ racist chanting and for fireworks offences during a Nations League match against France in 2025. Croatia have played Fifa-sanctioned World Cup qualifiers and friendlies at home in front of fans since but tonight is the first in Uefa competition and hence the ban.

However, a caveat in Uefa’s disciplinary regulations allows the home federation in such circumstances to fill the ground to 75 per cent of its capacity with “children up to the age of 14 (duly accompanied) from schools and/or football academies invited to the match free of charge”. And given the scrum outside the stadium this afternoon, that is what is happening.

Advertisement | GambleAware | 18+ Betting on the football tonight? Take a look at these tips and offers chosen by Telegraph Media Group

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of England’s Uefa Nations League Group A3 match against Croatia in Rijeka. Matches between the two are relatively frequent – 12 in 30 years. Croatia have beaten England three times in the 10 competitive meetings, home and away in qualification for Euro 2008, which dealt the England manager a blow from which he could not recover, and the World Cup semi-final in Moscow in 2018.

The extraordinary thing about both the first two defeats – the ‘Wally with the Brolly’ match in November 2007, Steve McLaren’s last in charge, and the home tie on October 10 2006 – is that Luka Modric played in both. And now eight days shy of 20 years since his first appearance against England, he is still running their midfield at the age of 41.

England have had the upper hand since Russia, winning in the Nations League at Wembley in 2018, opening their Euro 2020 campaign with a 1-0 victory by virtue of Raheem Sterling’s goal and then in June when they were at their fluent best, a rare occurrence, in the second half of their first World Cup group game to push on from 2-2 to finish 4-2.

Slaven Bilic, manager from 2006-12, is back in charge for his second spell but his squad still relies heavily on experienced players. Modric is the eldest but is joined by greybeard stalwarts Ivan Perisic, Ante Budimir and Andrej Kramaric, both 35. Spain hammered them 4-1 in midweek after they had started with a 2-1 victory over Czech Republic in Prague.

England, who rattled Spain and should have gone 3-1 up but lost 3-2, were much better in the second half in Prague against a team reduced to 10 men and deserved their 2-0 win, have played at the tiny Stadion Rujevica (capacity 8,279) once before, drawing 0-0 in 2018.

Thomas Tuchel, who changed three of his back four on Tuesday, may stick with Lewis Hall after he made a positive impression in combination with Anthony Gordon. As for Trent Alexander-Arnold, who set up the first goal, Tuchel does not go out of his way to undermine the perception that for all his unique quality, he just doesn’t fancy the Real Madrid right-back at all.

It’s up to Alexander-Arnold to make a compelling case if picked today or at Wembley on Tuesday to persuade the German head coach not to restore his beloved if brittle ‘Reecey’ James at the first opportunity.

#1449. Australian football rocked by allegations players fixed matches and illegally bet on their own games

Published: 05:28 EDT, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 05:28 EDT, 6 November 2026

Football Australia is investigating allegations that players registered with an Adelaide soccer club manipulated matches and illegally gambled on their own games during the 2026 season.

The Cove FC has responded to the reports by stating the club itself is not under investigation, and that the allegations concern 'a very small number of individuals' registered with the club.

The Trott Park club, in Adelaide's southern suburbs, released a statement on Friday after reports emerged of the integrity probe.

Football SA has confirmed an investigation involving players registered with Cove during the 2026 season, with Football Australia handling the matter.

'The Club wishes to make clear that The Cove FC itself is not under investigation,' chairman Phil Hole said in the statement.

'The allegations concern a very small number of individuals registered with the Club during the 2026 season.'

Players registered with The Cove FC during the 2026 season are the subject of an ongoing Football Australia integrity investigation

The probe reportedly concerns allegations of match-fixing and illegal betting on players' own games

According to News Corp, the allegations involve competition manipulation and illegal betting on the players' own matches.

No individuals or specific fixtures have been publicly identified in the supplied statements, and no findings or penalties have been announced.

Football Australia told 10 News Adelaide that its disciplinary process was ongoing and it would not comment further while its integrity unit worked through the matter.

Hole said Cove had cooperated with the national governing body throughout the investigation.

'The Cove FC takes matters of sporting integrity extremely seriously and has cooperated promptly and fully with Football Australia since becoming aware of the allegations and throughout the investigative process,' he said.

'The Club respects the ongoing investigative process and will not comment further at this stage.'

Football SA said Football Australia had exclusive jurisdiction to investigate the alleged integrity breaches, and that the state body would assist if requested.

'Cove FC have been fully cooperative and supportive of the investigation by Football Australia,' Football SA said.

Chairman Phil Hole says Cove has cooperated fully with Football Australia throughout the investigative process

'While the investigation remains active, Football SA is unable to provide details about the allegations or the parties involved.'

Daily Mail has contacted South Australian Police for comment.

Founded in 1983, Cove operates from the Southern Soccer Facility at Trott Park and has more than 800 members.

Its senior teams compete at semi-professional level, while the club also provides junior, women's, amateur, masters and inclusive football programs.

Hole said the club remained focused on its members and community while the investigation continued.

'We remain firmly committed to the values, standards and sporting integrity that underpin our Club,' he said.

'Our focus remains on our members, our community and building on the positive progress and success of The Cove FC.'
